queries.query: Find a scene where one character appears to have a choice but another character controls the situation.
queries.human_notes: Top hit scene-6 (21.52-23.69s) and the rest of the list are revolver/barman close-ups in the opening credits into the narrator's opening monologue. No scene in this window shows one character making a choice while another controls the situation. TF-IDF matched generic words (choice/control/character) in vision fields without any narrative reasoning; all scores sit near the floor (0.05-0.12).

queries.query: Find the strongest moment of tension between two characters.
queries.human_notes: scene-4 (18.31s revolver close-up) and scene-29 (86.21s bar monologue) rank high, and scene-30 (95.64-101.81s, the narrator with the gun at his mouth -- arguably the tensest beat in the window) appears 4th at 0.0338. Genuinely tense scenes do surface, but the strongest is not ranked first and the score gap is thin (0.0696 -> 0.0312).

queries.query: Find a scene where the meaning comes mostly from what characters do rather than what they say.
queries.human_notes: Top hits scene-10 (30.78s) and scene-8 (25.28s) are dialogue/monologue face-and-revolver close-ups where the meaning arrives from speech, not action. The window (title sequence + opening monologue) has no strong action-over-dialogue beat, so the query with no shared vocabulary scores at the floor.

queries.query: Find a moment where an important object is visually emphasized.
queries.human_notes: scene-25 (63.94-65.73s, a glowing blue object in extreme close-up, 0.1555 -- the highest single score in the whole eval), scene-15 (41.79s) and scene-4 (18.31s revolver close-up) all center on the revolver/object the cinematography actually emphasizes. This is the one query where the object emphasis genuinely matches on-screen framing.

queries.query: Find a scene that demonstrates the protagonist's relationship with fate.
queries.human_notes: Top hits scene-8 (25.28s), scene-19 (51.38s), scene-17 (46.13s) are monologue/revolver fragments; nothing in this window dramatizes a relationship with fate. Thematic query with no shared vocabulary, so TF-IDF returns floor-scoring word-overlap noise.

queries.query: Find a scene where a character's behavior contradicts what they say.
queries.human_notes: scene-10 (30.78s), scene-8 (25.28s), scene-31 (101.81s) are speaking/face shots whose transcript affirms what the character does (e.g. 'can't talk with a gun in your mouth'); there is no contradiction beat in the window. Word-level overlap produces this ranking, not understanding of intent.

queries.query: Who is present in this scene and what are they doing?
queries.human_notes: The richest who-is-present-and-doing-what content (scene-30 man holding a gun to his mouth, scene-31 blood visible on the face) exists in the index, but the rankings (scene-8/19/17/25) reward token overlap with the credits close-ups. The information is present in the vision fields; the ranking itself is keyword-driven and misses it.

queries.query: When does the most important visual event occur?
queries.human_notes: The most important visual event in the window is the gun-to-mouth reveal (~95.6-104s, scenes 30-31); retrieval returned scene-15 (41.79s), scene-5 (19.44s), scene-3 (16.98s logo). Also underlines the temporal weakness: a 'when' query gets no time-anchored answer with this lexicon-based retrieval.
